tokyo_sizzler_shinjuku_mitsui_.price_note: No items recorded, and it was chased hard before giving up: the chain publishes a full set of menu PDFs (grand, weekday lunch, drink, kids, weekend morning salad bar, takeaway) and THE GRAND MENU PDF HAS NO TEXT LAYER — 4.3MB of images, zero characters extracted. The Tabelog menu page carries nothing. That is the sixth unreadable menu in two shards, and this one is the most frustrating, because a chain this size almost certainly holds real allergen data internally. ⚠ WHY THIS RECORD IS WORTH HAVING EVEN EMPTY: a PREMIUM SALAD BAR is structurally one of the best formats in this entire dataset for a vegan, and among the better ones for a coeliac — raw vegetables and fruit carry no wheat and nothing animal, and unlike a set course you choose every component yourself. ⚠ AND WHY IT IS ALSO ONE OF THE RISKIEST: a buffet is SHARED TONGS. Croutons, pasta salad, dressings thickened with flour and a bread station all sit on the same counter, and a serving spoon moved between two trays undoes any amount of careful choosing. For a coeliac the bar is not "safe because it is vegetables"; it is safe only per-item and only if the tongs are. Sizzler is also known for its cheese toast, which is wheat. The chain ran an Aloha! Hawaiian Fair 15 July – 23 September 2026 with grilled items, coconut water and deli salads. Weekend morning salad bar 08:00–10:00 at selected branches; weekday lunch 11:00–15:00.

tokyo_asakusa_tsurujiro_okonom.price_note: ⚠ THE SHOP'S OWN DOMAIN DOES NOT RESOLVE. tsurujirou-asakusa.com fails DNS from two different resolvers — WebFetch returns ETIMEOUT and curl reports "Could not resolve host". Worth stating the distinction precisely rather than overclaiming: the resolver answer is SERVFAIL, a server failure, NOT NXDOMAIN — so unlike オーガニックごはん かえもん or とうふ川風, this is not confirmed as a deleted domain. It may be a broken or lapsed nameserver configuration rather than a domain that no longer exists, and it may come back. Recorded so a link-checker treats it as unresolved rather than as proof of closure, and so nobody reads it as a closure signal: nothing here says the restaurant has shut. The Tabelog menu page also carries no items, so there is no menu from any source. ⚠ THE CATEGORY ANSWER IS FIRM AND WORTH KEEPING EVEN WITH NO ITEMS: this is a もんじゃ焼き・お好み焼き・鉄板焼き house, and both house dishes are WHEAT BATTER by definition — okonomiyaki is wheat flour, egg, dashi and cabbage, and monjayaki is the same batter thinned with more liquid, not a different flour. The sauce is a Worcester-style brown sauce, the finish is katsuobushi and aonori, the mayonnaise is egg, and the griddle is shared with every order at the table. Some okonomiyaki kitchens will make a 山芋 batter on request; nothing published here suggests it, and there is currently no site on which to check.

tokyo_marugoto_hokkaido_asakus.price_note: PROVISIONAL and COURSES ONLY. The restaurant's own page carries no menu, the Tabelog menu page carries nothing, and what follows comes from the shop's Gnavi listing, which publishes its course plans but not its à la carte board. ⚠ WATCH THE TAX BASIS — IT IS INCONSISTENT ON THE SHOP'S OWN LISTING: the crab all-you-can-eat is quoted 税抜 (before tax), the Genghis Khan course appears as both ¥5,000 税別 and ¥5,500 税込 for what reads as the same plan, and the banquet course is quoted without a basis at all. Treat every figure as approximate and confirm when booking. ⚠ ON BOTH DIETS: this is a Hokkaido crab and lamb house, so there is nothing for a vegan. For a coeliac the structure is better than it looks — crab and grilled lamb are not floured, so the wheat is concentrated in the DIPS AND SAUCES rather than the food, which makes it a place where one question at the table changes several answers. Cancellation terms are unusually specific: ¥4,000 a head for a no-show on the day, ¥1,500 if you call, nothing the day before.

items.en: All-you-can-eat snow crab — the shop bills it as making the most of Hokkaido crab
items.note: Quoted 税抜 — BEFORE tax — so roughly ¥8,778 at the till. Steamed or boiled crab is one of the cleanest things a coeliac can eat: shellfish and water, with no coating and no marinade. What is not stated is what it is served WITH — ponzu is citrus plus SOY SAUCE, and a vinegared 三杯酢 normally contains soy too. Ask for lemon or salt. Crab rules out vegan.

items.ja: ジンギスカンコース（90分飲み放題付き）
items.en: Genghis Khan course with 90 minutes of free drinks — the shop names Hokkaido-direct fresh lamb shoulder loin; a further 30 minutes of drinks is +¥500
items.note: Listed as ¥5,000 税別 in one place and ¥5,500 税込 in another for what appears to be the same plan. ジンギスカン is lamb grilled over a domed pan and eaten with a tare, and Genghis Khan tare is a soy-sauce-and-fruit sauce — soy sauce is wheat by default. Some shops serve the lamb plain for salting instead, which is the question worth asking. The free-drink package is also beer-led, and BEER IS BARLEY, which Japanese allergen labelling does not cover.

The shop quotes 3,135円〜 without stating whether tax is included. Contents are not published; a banquet course at a Hokkaido house will centre on the same lamb and crab, and a set course removes the ability to decline anything. ジンギスカン is lamb grilled over a domed pan and eaten with a tare, and Genghis Khan tare is a soy-sauce-and-fruit sauce — soy sauce is wheat by default. Some shops serve the lamb plain for salting instead, which is the question worth asking.

tokyo_green_italian_torcia.price_note: ⚠ THIS RESTAURANT RUNS A VEGAN MENU AND MARKS ALLERGENS ON ITS PRINTED MENU — AND PUBLISHES NEITHER IN READABLE FORM. Both facts are worth having anyway, because they change how you'd approach the room. The shop states 「TORCIAはヴィーガンメニュー（植物性食材使用のメニュー）をさまざまなイタリアンに形を変えてご提供」 — a vegan menu carried across the Italian repertoire rather than one token dish — and frames the whole concept as 「あらゆる食の志向をもった人々が同じテーブルを囲んでお食事を楽しめる」, people with different diets sharing one table. On the menu pages it also states 「原材料に特定・推奨アレルギーが含まれる場合［ ］内に記載しています」: the STATUTORY AND RECOMMENDED ALLERGENS ARE PRINTED IN BRACKETS AGAINST EACH ITEM. That is rare in Tokyo and means the information a coeliac needs exists — on paper, in the restaurant. ⚠ AND THE CAVEAT THE SHOP VOLUNTEERS ITSELF: 「当店キッチンは動物性食材も取り扱っております」 — the kitchen handles animal ingredients, so the vegan menu is a recipe promise, not a separate kitchen. It also says to tell staff about allergies. WHY THERE IS ONLY ONE ITEM BELOW: every menu — dinner courses, à la carte, dolce, lunch, afternoon tea — is published as a JPG (lunch2.jpg … afternoon.jpg) with no text layer and no useful alt attributes, and the Tabelog menu page carries nothing. The single course price is the only figure stated in text anywhere. Lunch 11:00–15:00 (courses and pasta sets), 15:00–17:00 dolce sets and afternoon tea.

items.en: Dinner course, from — choose an antipasto and a pasta and combine as you like; the shop states a vegan version is available, and recommends wine pairing
items.note: The only price the site states in text (税込). Both axes are genuinely open rather than unknown-by-default, which is unusual: the shop says a VEGAN version of the course exists, so a plant-based build is offered rather than improvised — but it also says the kitchen handles animal ingredients, so shared equipment is a live question. On gluten, an Italian course means pasta and bread by default; what makes this askable rather than a flat no is that the printed menu carries bracketed allergen marks per item, so the answer is available at the table even though it is not online. Ask for the ヴィーガン course and read the brackets.

tokyo_matsue_shibuya_scramble_.price_note: No menu recorded. The shop's own site has 昼のメニュー, 夜のメニュー and お飲物 sections and its /menu/ page returns 200 — but not one dish or price is present as text on any of them, and the Tabelog menu page carries nothing either. ⚠ WHAT IS ESTABLISHED ABOUT THE SHAPE OF A MEAL HERE: the shop describes itself as centring on an OMAKASE COURSE that opens with seasonal tsumami — sashimi and grilled dishes — before the sushi, with a cheaper lunch also offered, and fish bought from Toyosu and the Hokkaido and Kyushu markets. ⚠ WHY THE OMAKASE FORMAT MATTERS FOR A COELIAC, as recorded at 鮨 奥 in shard s10: you do not choose, courses arrive one at a time already dressed, and at an Edomae counter the chef brushes 煮切り — reduced SOY SAUCE — onto the fish before it reaches you, so the wheat arrives without being ordered and there is no dipping bowl to decline. The 焼き物 that open the course are a second route, since grilled fish that is not salt-grilled is normally soy-marinated. The conversation has to happen when booking, not at the counter. Nothing here suits a vegan — it is a fish counter. Closed irregularly, following Shibuya Scramble Square.

tokyo_kielo_coffee_asakusa.price_note: No café menu published. The record's stored website is the roaster's ONLINE BEAN SHOP — a storefront selling coffee beans by the bag, with collections, a shipping policy and a shop list — and the shop-list page carries addresses, hours and Instagram links for four Tokyo branches but no drink, no food and no price. The Tabelog menu page carries nothing. So the empty list is the honest answer: this is a shop whose e-commerce site is not its café menu. ⚠ FOR BOTH DIETS, THE ORIENTATION IS SIMPLE AND WORTH STATING: black coffee is roasted bean and water — no wheat, nothing animal — so the espresso side of a specialty café is one of the few categories that suits both diets by default. Everything after that is a question. MILK is the vegan one and no plant alternative is mentioned anywhere on the site, which for a Nordic-style specialty roaster would be unusual to lack but is not something to assume. The BAKERY is the gluten one: a Nordic-inspired bakery counter means cardamom buns, rye and pastry, all wheat by default, and 天然酵母 or 全粒粉 framing would not change that — as recorded at ぱん屋 in shard s14, those describe the leavening and the milling, not the absence of wheat. Nothing here is recorded as an item because nothing is sourced.
